item.title: Go Daily Question 20250608
item.description:
What is the output of the following code? Why?

package main

import "fmt"

type Foo struct {
    bar string
}

func main() {
    s1 := []Foo{
        {"A"},
        {"B"},
        {"C"},
    }
    s2 := make([]*Foo, len(s1))
    for i, value := range s1 {
        s2[i] = &value
    }
    fmt.Println(s1[0], s1[1], s1[2])
    fmt.Println(s2[0], s2[1], s2[2])
}

// Output:
// {A} {B} {C}
// &{A} &{B} &{C}

item.title: Go Daily Question 104
item.description:
Is the output of the following code correct?

type Foo struct {
    bar string
}
func main() {
    s1 := []Foo{
        {"A"},
        {"B"},
        {"C"},
    }
    s2 := make([]*Foo, len(s1))
    for i, value := range s1 {
        s2[i] = &value
    }
    fmt.Println(s1[0], s1[1], s1[2])
    fmt.Println(s2[0], s2[1], s2[2])
}
Output:
{A} {B} {C}
&{A} &{B} &{C}
🔑 Answer Analysis:

After Go 1.22, the output is normal. Before Go 1.22: The for range loop reuses the value variable. The address of value is the same throughout, so the output for s2 would become CCC.

item.title: Go Daily Question 099
item.description:
What is the output of the following code? Why?

func main() {

    var m = [...]int{1, 2, 3}

    for i, v := range m {
        go func() {
            fmt.Println(i, v)
        }()
    }

    time.Sleep(time.Second * 3)
}
🔑 Answer Analysis:

Before Go 1.22, the output would be: 2 3 2 3 2 3 The for range loop uses short variable declaration (:=) to iterate variables. It’s important to note that variables i and v are reused in each loop iteration, not re-declared.

item.title: Go Daily Question 027
item.description:

}

    // Define map

    // Define student array

        {Name: "zhou", Age: 24},
        {Name: "li", Age: 23},
        {Name: "wang", Age: 22},
    }

    // Add array elements to map one by one
    for _, stu := range stus {
        m[stu.Name] = &stu
    }

    // Print map
    for k,v := range m {
        fmt.Println(k ,"=>", v.Name)
    }
}

Note that this type of problem will change in Go versions after 1.22.
